questions.background: This question concerns the five-on-five basketball tournament, rather than the separate three-on-three competition.

Resolution : Resolve to the country that wins the bronze-medal match in the men's basketball tournament at the 2026 Asian Games, once the final result is announced. Leaving 29% unallocated accounts for Lebanon, Chinese Taipei, Jordan (2023 silver), Saudi Arabia, and Qatar.

questions.background: British authorities have been investigating allegations involving Rwandan genocide suspects living in the United Kingdom.

Resolution : Identify the first individual formally charged in the United Kingdom in connection with alleged involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide, provided the charges are announced by December 31, 2026. Arrests without charges, extradition proceedings, and charges brought outside the United Kingdom do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The person’s full name as given in the charging announcement.
questions.current_reasoning: Scotland Yard's War Crimes Team has investigated six Rwandan genocide suspects in the UK since 2018 and confirmed in December 2025 that two investigations are at an advanced stage with full files submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service (one submitted in late 2023, a second by late 2025), while none had been charged as of May 2026. The two CPS files almost certainly come from the four named suspects interviewed voluntarily in 2020—Celestin Mutabaruka (Kent), Celestin Ugirashebuja (Essex), Emmanuel Nteziryayo (Manchester), and Dr. Vincent Bajinya, who legally changed his name to Vincent Brown (London)—whereas fifth suspect Charles Munyaneza (Bedford) suffered a stroke and was only interviewed in 2024, and a sixth suspect arrested in Gateshead in January 2024 remains publicly unnamed. Splitting Bajinya's ~20% share between his UK legal name 'Vincent Brown' (11%) and birth name 'Vincent Bajinya' (9%) reflects CPS charging announcement naming conventions while leaving 19% for Munyaneza and unnamed suspects.

questions.title: Which former minister from Viktor Orban's government, if any, will have parliamentary immunity lifted in September 2026 to permit an embezzlement investigation?
questions.background: The party that won Hungary's 2026 parliamentary election campaigned on tackling corruption. Parliamentary immunity can prevent prosecutors from pursuing criminal investigations against legislators unless Parliament lifts it.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Hungarian parliamentary records or contemporaneous reporting from reliable news organizations identifying former ministers whose immunity is lifted. Qualifying Event : Hungary's Parliament must vote during September 2026 to remove a former Orban-government minister's immunity specifically to allow prosecutors to pursue an embezzlement investigation. Allegations alone, without the parliamentary vote, do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : Provide the former minister's full name. If no former minister qualifies during September 2026, resolve as no qualifying minister.
questions.current_reasoning: Following Péter Magyar's Tisza party winning a two-thirds parliamentary supermajority in April 2026, Viktor Orbán relinquished his parliamentary seat in May (removing him from immunity votes), while the new government launched five parliamentary investigative committees and 'Operation Cleansing Fire' (NVVH asset-recovery office) and prosecutors began opening new corruption cases. However, lifting a sitting MP's immunity specifically during September 2026 for an embezzlement investigation requires prosecutorial action within a narrow one-month window, keeping 'no qualifying minister' highly plausible at 42%. Among former Orbán ministers retaining parliamentary seats, Antal Rogán (22%) is the prime target—personally named by Magyar on May 15 and overseeing centralized government communications tied to the June 13 €3.5B Integrity Authority scandal—followed by János Lázár (11%), Péter Szijjártó (9%), and Gergely Gulyás (6%).

questions.background: The Artemis Accords establish principles for international cooperation in civil space exploration.

Reaching #75 by September 27 (coinciding with UNGA High-Level Week) requires eight additional signings from 40+ plausible non-signatory U.S.-aligned states, so predicting which exact country lands specifically on slot #75 is highly diffuse—each leading candidate carries roughly a 4–6% marginal probability, and proper Brier Skill Score optimization requires not inflating top-5 probabilities.
